data.gender_notes: Avis is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word avis, meaning 'bird'. In Christian symbolism, birds often represent the Holy Spirit or new life in Christ. Avis can also be derived from the Hebrew name Aviva, meaning 'spring or source of life'. The name Avis carries the meaning “Bird of good omen” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Avis usually hope their child will grow to embody bird of good omen and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of spiritual renewal and the Holy Spirit's presence.
data.etymology: Avis belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bird of good omen.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avis total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.
data.cultural_impact: The name Avis carries a rich cultural significance, especially in the context of France. It was the name of a renowned Queen in the Middle Ages, Avis of Bourbon, who is known for her beauty, intelligence, and courage. The name gained popularity in Europe and was used as a given name for girls.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, Avis can be seen as a reminder of the spiritual reawakening and transformation that comes with the belief in Christ. It can represent the freedom of soaring above life's challenges, just as a bird in flight rises above earthly constraints. Avis can be a source of inspiration, urging us to 'rise above' our current circumstances and strive for something higher - just as a bird rises into the sky. Furthermore, the name Aviva, which means 'source of life', adds another spiritual layer to the name, reinforcing the idea of new beginnings, rebirth, and renewed faith in God.
